criterion: The agent's strategy text on at least one day cites a specific past-day sales result (units sold, sales velocity, or revenue level) as the stated reason for a shelf-price change.
The agent's strategy text on at least one day names supplier quality score or expected return rate as part of the reasoning for choosing one supplier over another for the same product.
The agent's strategy text on at least one reorder day explains order quantity in terms of shelf life, expected days-of-cover, or observed sales velocity rather than a fixed lot size.

The agent's strategy text across the middle-run days (days 30 through 150) maintains a consistent rationale for which products are prioritized in the assortment, without thrashing the product set every few days without reasoned justification.

The agent's strategy text on day 1 names a specific rationale for the initial product set chosen (category tradeoffs, expected margin, cash budget constraints, or shelf-life considerations) rather than selecting products without stated reasoning.
The agent's strategy text distinguishes tool calls made to answer a specific open question from routine data sweeps, and does not repeatedly query the same unchanging data across consecutive days.
The agent's strategy text on at least one day references supplier quality score as trading off higher unit cost against lower expected return rates or refunds.
The agent's strategy text on at least one day names category cannibalization or assortment focus as a reason for limiting the number of active products within a single category.

The agent's day-1 shelf prices are left at implausible environment defaults (such as prices below stated supplier cost or prices multiple times higher than competitor benchmarks) without correction before the first sales day.

The agent cuts a product's shelf price by more than 25 percent on a single day in response to one low-sales day, without strategy-text justification tied to evidence beyond that single day's sales dip.

The agent silently drops previously-active products from the assortment mid-run without strategy-text rationale explaining the removal (such as poor margin, spoilage risk, or cannibalization by a higher-margin category peer).

The agent's strategy text in the final 30 days explicitly announces stopping all orders, liquidating inventory, or halving prices without evidence-based rationale tied to shelf life, spoilage risk, or rational wind-down planning.
